extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants and institutional research administrators (especially foreign institutions applying to NIAID G11 awards) and NIH review staff
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and reviewer critique for an NIAID G11 (Global Infectious Disease Research Administration Development Award) application, showing the review criteria, strengths/weaknesses noted by reviewers, and administrative/eligibility considerations relevant to applicants and administrators. Useful for preparing or responding to NIH peer review for similar capacity-building awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? Reviewers evaluate the importance of the problem, the magnitude of potential effect, and whether the project will improve institutional capacity and produce sustainable benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of strengths cited: clear strategy to institutionalize NIH grants management best practices; clear picture of current infrastructure; training focused on closing identified post-award gaps; involvement of experienced external trainer (Kathleen Fisher) and planned site visit. Examples of weaknesses cited: lack of projected number of research administrators and institutions that will benefit; absence of defined indicators to measure and verify that learning occurred and gaps were closed; training overly focused on post-award with little pre-award content (may reflect needs assessment). Reviewers expect explicit metrics for impact and reach when significance claims are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD(s)/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? Reviewers consider the investigators' experience, expertise, resources, and authority to implement institutional changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: PI has relevant administrative authority and experience, membership in professional organizations, prior training experience, and access to NIH grants management resources; strong collaborating personnel including an administrative coordinator with QA responsibilities; Yale trainer oversight. Weaknesses noted: missing biosketch for a key US collaborator (Kathleen Fisher) and omission from key personnel profiles can weaken confidence. Reviewers look for documented qualifications and clear assignments of roles/effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application propose novel concepts, approaches, or interventions? For capacity-building awards, reviewers assess whether proposed approaches represent meaningful advances or creative adaptations that increase sustainability and regional applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths cited: leveraging existing library/documentation systems; translating materials to Spanish; developing online components and an in-house grant-tracking system; use of webinars and videoconferencing; inclusion of Yale leadership courses for administrators. Weaknesses cited: concerns about regional IT/internet robustness hindering online delivery; limited evidence of Train-the-Trainer preparation at Yale; unclear whether similar Spanish materials already exist. Innovation can be in sustainability and adaptation rather than technological novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims? For training/capacity-building projects this includes curriculum design, implementation plans, timelines, needs assessment linkage, evaluation methods, and contingency planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths noted: well-articulated, logical sequence of activities (US training followed by internal implementation and dissemination), clear methodologies, credible timetable, rigorous needs assessment, and strong documentation of available IT and videoconferencing resources (SharePoint, OneDrive, Zoom, YouTube archive). Weaknesses noted: insufficient plans/details for assessing impact on external institutions; lack of contingency/alternative plans for power outages/internet failures; unclear description and roll-out plan for the administrative tracking system; timing/synchronization issues between trainings and SOP/system implementation; insufficient long-range cost model for training external institutions. Reviewers expect concrete evaluation metrics, rollout plans, and contingency strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific and institutional environment contribute to the probability of success? Reviewers consider institutional commitment, available resources, oversight and compliance structures, and collaborative arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengths cited: strong institutional compliance infrastructure (IRBs, advisory committees), diverse research support units (biostatistics, clinical research, ethics, admin), documented IT/network and videoconferencing facilities, institutional commitment from leadership. Weaknesses cited: unclear internet/power reliability for external beneficiaries; no identified funding for long-term maintenance/enhancement of grants management system. Applicants should document institutional support, commitments of facilities/staff, and sustainability funding or plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall impact reflects reviewers' assessment of the project's likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field or institutional capacity. Reviewers summarize the combined judgment across criteria and assign an impact/priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement gives an integrative narrative of strengths and weaknesses leading to the final impact judgment (e.g., 'outstanding application with only a few minor weaknesses'). Reviewers expect a clear logic connecting aims, methods, personnel, environment, and sustainability to an overall assessment. Use the résumé/summary to understand how reviewer concerns influenced the final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring process and numeric calculation of impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers' scores are collected and how the impact/priority score is calculated (procedural).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores (1-9) are submitted by assigned reviewers prior to the meeting and are not discussed or mathematically combined into the overall impact score at the meeting. The overall impact/priority score is calculated by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Some applications may also receive a percentile ranking. See NIH peer review process documentation (link given in statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess protections for human subjects when applicable (risk minimization, inclusion/exclusion, informed consent, data safety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application the category is marked 'NOT APPLICABLE.' For applicable projects, reviewers expect a full human subjects protection plan addressing regulatory and ethical safeguards; absence of applicable issues must be explicitly stated. Protection of human subjects is a separate review consideration noted in the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess plans for inclusion of women where human subjects research is involved or note applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'NOT APPLICABLE' here. When applicable, reviewers expect clear recruitment and analysis plans addressing sex/gender balance and justification for any exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess plans for inclusion of minority groups in human subjects research or note applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'NOT APPLICABLE' here. When applicable, include recruitment and retention plans and analysis strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Individuals Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider whether the inclusion of participants across age ranges is appropriate or justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'NOT APPLICABLE' for this application. Provide justification if certain age groups are excluded in applicable studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the use of vertebrate animals when included in the proposal (justification, welfare, procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application notes 'NOT APPLICABLE.' For applicable proposals, include a detailed vertebrate animals plan addressing care, use, and justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data, Model Organisms, Genomic Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers note and comment on data sharing plans, model organism sharing, and genomic data sharing when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this summary the Data Sharing Plan, Model Organism Sharing Plan, and Genomic Data Sharing Plan are marked 'NOT APPLICABLE.' When relevant, applicants must provide clear plans for sharing or justify limitations; reviewers will comment and NIH may factor these plans into funding decisions or award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: For foreign institutions, reviewers and staff evaluate whether foreign institution participation is justified and appropriate for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application lists 'FOREIGN INSTITUTION: JUSTIFIED' with comment 'Colombia.' Applicants must provide justification for foreign institutional eligibility, demonstrate adequate institutional infrastructure and address any additional compliance or administrative considerations for foreign grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess plans for authentication of critical biological and chemical resources when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'NOT APPLICABLE' in this summary. If applicable, applicants should include methods and procedures to ensure identity and validity of key resources (cell lines, antibodies, reagents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers/staff check whether proposed budgetary items overlap with other funding sources or result in duplication of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked 'NOT APPLICABLE' here. The summary also contains an ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET NOTE: the budget shown is the applicant's requested budget and may be adjusted by grants management staff based on committee recommendations. If an award is planned, costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff per the COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The review committee may provide budget recommendations which inform grants management calculations and award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case 'The budget is recommended as requested in all years.' The administrative budget note clarifies that reviewers' budget recommendations guide but do not themselves set final award amounts — grants management calculates final costs based on recommendations.
